items.title: Sim console: lazy-load the honesty rails and bound them (no planet walk in a request)
items.detail: Measured 2026-09-14 on box E: GET /simworld answers a guest in 94 s and the page polls every 2 s. SimConsoleController::world() runs three planet-wide rails on every request: a count of active district maps, the over-bound chambers (Type B above Type A) and the seat-gap chambers (a correlated SUM of drawn district seats for every chamber with an active map). Operator ruling 2026-09-14: fix the load with pagination or lazy loading, no cache, no scheduler.
items.done_when: The page renders its live bars without the rails; the rails come from their own endpoint requested once after mount, each bounded: over-bound is an indexed predicate with a 25-row page, the active-map figure is an indexed count, and the seat gap compares Type A seats with a drawn-seat total stored on the map row by the districting engine (additive migration, written at draw time), so no request sums districts across the planet. GET /simworld answers a guest in under 2 s on box E; the sweep establishes the route and reports zero nodes; a pin asserts the query shapes.

Guest GET /simworld 94 s to 0.8 s. Triggers proven on a disposable database (map_drawn_seats_trigger_check: 9 checks). Sweep alone in Edge: PASS 19.1 s. Pinned by SimConsoleRailsTest (3).
